nodes.label: Handbook of CRM: Achieving Excellence in Customer Management
Customer Relationship Management (CRM)
nodes.rationale: Defined as a strategic approach creating shareholder value via appropriate relationships with key customers and segments; 'information-enabled relationship marketing'. Strategic view preferred because narrow IT-only views drive the widely reported CRM project failures.

nodes.label: Relationship Marketing
nodes.rationale: CRM builds on RM principles: retention of profitable customers, multiple market domains, cross-functional marketing.

nodes.label: Customer Lifetime Value
nodes.rationale: Future flow of net profit discounted to present attributable to a customer; forces recognition that customers are not equally profitable.

nodes.label: Command and Control Organizational Structure
nodes.rationale: Functional silos push customers aside; contrasted with cross-functional CRM processes.

nodes.label: Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP)
nodes.rationale: Back-office efficiency vs CRM front-office effectiveness.

nodes.label: Learning Relationship
nodes.rationale: Mass customization plus one-to-one marketing bind producer and consumer; creates switching costs.

nodes.label: CRM Continuum (Three Perspectives of CRM)
nodes.rationale: From narrow tactical (single tech project) to broad strategic (holistic approach to shareholder value); book advocates the strategic end.

nodes.label: Relationship Marketing / CRM / Customer Management Hierarchy
CRM Application and Service Provider Segments (Gartner)
Strategic Framework for CRM
nodes.rationale: Five interacting, iterative cross-functional processes; implementation starts with strategy and ends with performance improvement.

nodes.label: Business Strategy
nodes.rationale: CRM does not own business strategy but must understand it and escalate when it is misdirected.

nodes.label: Seven Best Practices for Making Vision and Values Work
Industry Analysis Framework (Eight Dimensions)
nodes.rationale: Augments Porter's five forces with co-opetition, environmental analysis and disruptive technologies.

nodes.label: Customer Intimacy
nodes.rationale: Considered the business strategy most appropriate to CRM principles.

nodes.label: Market Segmentation
nodes.rationale: Over 50% of successful strategy assignments were based on creative segmentation; recommends value/benefit-based segmentation first.

nodes.label: CRM Strategy Matrix
nodes.rationale: Axes: completeness of customer information vs degree of customer individualization.

nodes.rationale: Lovelock's eight clusters operationalize the total value offer; competition shifts to supplementary services as cores commoditize.

Trade-off Analysis
nodes.rationale: Measures attribute importance without direct rating, forces trade-offs, per customer

nodes.label: Customer Profitability
nodes.rationale: Customers, not products, create profits; costs after production differ by customer

nodes.label: Customer Profitability Analysis
nodes.rationale: Assign all account-specific costs using the avoidability principle

nodes.label: Avoidability Principle
nodes.rationale: Ask which costs would be avoided if we did not do business with the customer

nodes.label: Most Valuable Customers (MVC)
nodes.rationale: CRM objective: retention

nodes.label: Second Tier Customers (STC)
nodes.rationale: CRM objective: growth

nodes.label: Below Zero Customers (BZ)
nodes.rationale: CRM objective: divestment

nodes.label: Acquisition Break-even
nodes.rationale: Acquisition cost divided by annual profit per customer gives years to break even

nodes.label: Reichheld and Sasser Retention Research
nodes.rationale: 5 point retention increase yields 25-95% NPV profit increase

nodes.label: Acquirers, Retainers and Profit Maximizers
nodes.rationale: 80% of firms over-spend on acquisition

nodes.label: Customer Retention Improvement Framework
nodes.rationale: Three steps: measure retention, identify root causes of defection, corrective action

nodes.label: Customer Lifetime Value (CLV)
nodes.rationale: NPV of future profit flows over the relationship incl. cross-sell, upsell, advocacy, reference

nodes.label: Reference Value
nodes.rationale: B2B customers acting as reference sites

nodes.label: ACURA Framework
nodes.rationale: Acquisition, cross-sell, upsell, retention, advocacy - systematic profit improvement

nodes.label: Value Statement
nodes.rationale: General statement of intent used to position BT

nodes.label: Zurich Financial Services Value Proposition Framework
nodes.rationale: Five processes: core development, develop, market test, launch, review

nodes.label: Multi-channel Integration Process
nodes.rationale: Translates strategy/value outputs into value-adding customer interactions

nodes.label: Strategic Framework for CRM
nodes.rationale: Five cross-functional processes

nodes.label: Channel Participants
nodes.rationale: Intermediaries: wholesalers, retailers, VARs

nodes.label: Channel Options
nodes.rationale: Channel media: sales force, branches, call centres, Internet

nodes.label: Buyer-oriented Intermediaries
nodes.rationale: Buying engines and communities

nodes.label: Six Channel Categories
nodes.rationale: Sales force, outlets, telephony, direct marketing, e-commerce, M-commerce

nodes.label: M-commerce
nodes.rationale: Time and place independent; location-based

nodes.label: Channel Strategy Options
nodes.rationale: Mono-channel, segment, graduated account mgmt, migrator, activity-based, integrated multi-channel

nodes.label: Customer Relationship Life-cycle
nodes.rationale: Acquisition, consolidation, enhancement

nodes.label: Customer Activity Cycle
nodes.rationale: Vandermerwe

nodes.label: Jones and Sasser Loyalty Study
nodes.rationale: Only 5/5 delighted customers are truly loyal

nodes.label: Perfect Customer Experience
nodes.rationale: 5/5 satisfaction at affordable cost, relative to expectations

nodes.label: Channel Chain Analysis
nodes.rationale: Wilson and McDonald

nodes.label: Information Management Process
nodes.rationale: Engine driving CRM: collect customer info and build profiles

nodes.label: CRM Strategy Matrix
nodes.rationale: Product-based selling, customer-based marketing, managed service and support, individualized CRM

nodes.label: Operational Data Store (ODS)
nodes.rationale: Single identity for customers, structured for transactional performance

nodes.label: Enterprise Data Model
nodes.rationale: Rules for cleansing, deduplication and combining data

nodes.label: OLAP
nodes.rationale: Historical reporting vs forward-looking data mining

nodes.label: Linkage Model (Service Profit Chain)
nodes.rationale: Leadership -> employee attitudes -> customer satisfaction -> financial performance

nodes.label: Key Drivers of Shareholder Results
nodes.rationale: Employee value, customer value, shareholder value, cost reduction

nodes.label: Cost Reduction
nodes.rationale: Must not reduce customer value

nodes.label: Shareholder Value Measures (EVA, SVA, MVA, CFROI)
CRM Metrics and KPIs
nodes.rationale: Metrics vs KPIs; customer, people/process, strategic, output metrics

nodes.label: Output and Comparative Metrics
nodes.rationale: Relative measures vs competitors matter more than absolute internal ones, which give an insular view.

nodes.label: Special E-Metrics
nodes.rationale: Despite rich web data, few companies use e-metrics to monitor e-CRM.

nodes.label: Malcolm Baldrige Award
nodes.rationale: Measures employee, customer and financial results but does not link them causally.

nodes.label: Balanced Scorecard
nodes.rationale: Four perspectives (customer, internal, innovation/learning, financial); must be tailored per company; mixed focus can weaken customer responsiveness.

nodes.label: Service-Profit Chain
nodes.rationale: Profit driven by loyalty, loyalty by satisfaction, satisfaction by value, value by satisfied productive employees, employee satisfaction by internal service quality.

nodes.label: Sears Roebuck and Company
nodes.rationale: 5-unit rise in employee attitude drives 1.3-unit rise in customer impression and 0.5 rise in revenue growth.

nodes.label: Nortel Networks
nodes.rationale: Employee satisfaction found to account for 52% of customer satisfaction; leadership 31% of employee satisfaction.

nodes.label: Success Map
nodes.rationale: Extension of strategy map stressing broader stakeholders and end goals; distils many measures to those that matter.

nodes.label: Barriers to CRM Success
nodes.rationale: Internal attitudes and structure are more common barriers than legacy systems.

nodes.label: Quick Wins Approach
nodes.rationale: Incremental visible benefits secure funding and buy-in; long projects risk cancellation (>3 years or no benefit in 18 months).

nodes.label: Benefits Dependency Network
nodes.rationale: Works backwards from objectives so business changes, not just technology, deliver benefits.

nodes.label: Hard vs Soft CRM Implementation
nodes.rationale: Henneberg: 16 of 23 firms took the hard IT/analytics route, often deriving strategy from IT processes, reversing best practice.

nodes.label: CRM Vendor Selection
nodes.rationale: Vendor stability matters; picking a marginally faster but unstable vendor led to costly migration.

nodes.label: CRM Pilot Projects
nodes.rationale: Pilots prove concept cheaply, reduce political risk and overcome lack of buy-in.

nodes.label: Recruit for Attitude Train for Skills
nodes.rationale: Technical skills are teachable; work ethic and psychological traits are less malleable.

nodes.label: CRM Budget
nodes.rationale: Budgets underfund change management, project management and employee engagement; data/technology are only ~25% of competency determinants.
